title: Keywords
content:
# Keywords

Read the Search keywords your Google campaigns run, add keywords to an ad group, and research new ones with the Keyword Planner.

import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

By the end of this page, you can:

- read the keywords your campaigns already run (synced, free to query)
- add keywords to an ad group
- research keywords you do not run yet (Keyword Planner, live against Google)

You need a `googleads` [account](/platforms/google-ads#connect).

## Synced keyword criteria

Call `GET /v1/ads/keywords`. It returns the Google Search keyword criteria (positive and negative) synced from connected accounts, one row per ad-group keyword.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
import Zernio from '@zernio/node';

const zernio = new Zernio();

const { data: synced } = await zernio.adcampaigns.listAdKeywords({
  query: {
    accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d',
    adAccountId: '1234567890',
    matchType: 'exact',
    negative: false,
    search: 'platform',
    limit: 100
  }
});

console.log(synced.keywords);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from zernio import Zernio

client = Zernio()

synced = client.ad_campaigns.list_ad_keywords(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    ad_account_id="1234567890",
    match_type="exact",
    negative=False,
    search="platform",
    limit=100,
)

print(synced["keywords"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/keywords?accountId=66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d&adAccountId=1234567890&matchType=exact&negative=false&search=platform&limit=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "keywords": [
    {
      "id": "66f2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2",
      "platformCriterionId": "987654321",
      "resourceName": "customers/1234567890/adGroupCriteria/165489732105~987654321",
      "platform": "google",
      "adAccountId": "1234567890",
      "campaignId": "21874563210",
      "campaignName": "US DevOps Search",
      "adSetId": "165489732105",
      "adSetName": "US DevOps Search",
      "keyword": "internal developer platform",
      "matchType": "exact",
      "status": "active",
      "negative": false,
      "qualityScore": 7,
      "metrics": { "windowDays": 30, "clicks": 84, "impressions": 2210, "cost": 61.4, "conversions": 3, "firstPageCpc": 0.42, "firstPositionCpc": 1.9 }
    }
  ],
  "pagination": { "page": 1, "limit": 100, "total": 1, "pages": 1 }
}
```

Filters:

- `campaignId`
- `adSetId` (the Google ad group)
- `status`
- `matchType`
- `negative` (`true` returns negative keywords only)
- `search` (a case-insensitive substring on the keyword text)

`metrics` is a trailing 30-day window in the account currency.

`qualityScore` is Google's 1 to 10 score, `null` when unrated. `quality` carries the same score plus its three component ratings.

Each row carries two ids:

- `id` is Zernio's keyword id.
- `platformCriterionId` is Google's `ad_group_criterion.criterion_id`, which is unique only within its ad group.

`resourceName` is Google's full resource name ending in `{adSetId}~{platformCriterionId}`. That tail is the keyword id Google itself uses.

Match that tail against GAQL rows. It is also what [labels](/platforms/google-ads/account-management#labels) take in `keywordIds`.

**Freshness.** The list refreshes about once a day per Google Ads customer.

The keyword sweep rides the ads discovery pass on a slower slot, so keywords added on Google can take up to a day to appear here.

A newly connected account is populated on its first discovery pass, and a manual sync refreshes it immediately.

Campaign-level negative keywords are not included, only ad-group-level criteria. Read those with `GET /v1/ads/campaigns/{campaignId}/negative-keywords`.

For live, current-state keyword data, query GAQL directly. See [Insights and GAQL](/platforms/google-ads/analytics#raw-gaql-queries).

## Add keywords to an ad group

Call `POST /v1/ads/keywords` with `accountId`, the ad group as `adSetId` and `keywords`. It adds to the ad group without touching the keywords already there.

`negative: true` adds ad-group-level negatives instead.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/keywords" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    "adSetId": "165489732105",
    "keywords": ["developer portal", { "text": "platform engineering", "matchType": "phrase" }]
  }'
```

Response (`201`), the same row shape as the list:

```json
{
  "keywords": [
    { "id": "66f2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e3", "adSetId": "165489732105", "keyword": "developer portal", "matchType": "broad", "status": "active", "negative": false },
    { "id": "66f2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e4", "adSetId": "165489732105", "keyword": "platform engineering", "matchType": "phrase", "status": "active", "negative": false }
  ]
}
```

To replace the whole set, send `targeting.keywords` or `targeting.negativeKeywords` on `PUT /v1/ads/{adId}`.

Each supplied list is the full desired set for the ad group, affecting sibling ads too.

Matching uses case-insensitive text plus match type. Omitting `matchType` means broad match.

- Unchanged criteria retain their IDs, status, bids, labels and history.
- Missing criteria are removed.
- Changing text or match type removes the old criterion and creates a new one.

## Change or remove one keyword

Pause or re-enable a single keyword with `PATCH /v1/ads/keywords/{keywordId}` ([Update keyword](/ad-campaigns/update-ad-keyword)). `status` is `active` or `paused`.

`keywordId` takes either form:

- the `id` from the list above
- Google's native `{adSetId}~{platformCriterionId}`, the tail of `resourceName` (for example `165489732105~987654321`)

A bare criterion id is rejected with a `400`, because it is only unique within its ad group.

Nothing else in the ad group is touched:

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/keywords/66f2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "status": "paused" }'
```

Response (`200`), the updated row:

```json
{
  "keyword": {
    "id": "66f2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2",
    "adSetId": "165489732105",
    "keyword": "internal developer platform",
    "matchType": "exact",
    "status": "paused",
    "negative": false
  }
}
```

`DELETE` on the same path ([Remove keyword](/ad-campaigns/remove-ad-keyword)) takes either id form. It removes the criterion from its ad group, positive or negative:

```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/keywords/165489732105~987654321" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "removed": true,
  "keywordId": "66f2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2",
  "platformCriterionId": "987654321",
  "resourceName": "customers/1234567890/adGroupCriteria/165489732105~987654321",
  "adSetId": "165489732105",
  "campaignId": "21874563210"
}
```

Google gives negative keywords no status, so `PATCH` on one returns `422`. Remove it instead.

A `404` means the `keywordId` is not a keyword on one of your connected accounts.

## Campaign negatives and shared lists

Campaign negatives are separate from the synced ad-group criteria.

[`GET /v1/ads/campaigns/{campaignId}/negative-keywords`](/ad-campaigns/list-campaign-negative-keywords) reads them. [`PUT` on the same path](/ad-campaigns/replace-campaign-negative-keywords) replaces the full desired `keywords` set, up to 1,000 entries.

Strings mean broad match. Objects accept `text` and `matchType`.

Send `keywords: []` to clear the campaign's negatives.

For negatives reused across campaigns, manage a shared list:

1. [`POST /v1/ads/accounts/negative-keyword-lists`](/ad-accounts/create-ad-negative-keyword-list) creates a list with `accountId`, `name` and optional `keywords` (up to 5,000). Include `customerId` when the connection has multiple customers. Creation does not attach the list to a campaign and is not idempotent.
2. [`GET` on that collection](/ad-accounts/list-ad-negative-keyword-lists) lists shared lists. [`GET /v1/ads/accounts/negative-keyword-lists/{listId}`](/ad-accounts/get-ad-negative-keyword-list) reads one with its keywords and criterion IDs; [`PUT` on that path](/ad-accounts/update-ad-negative-keyword-list) renames it.
3. [`PUT /v1/ads/accounts/negative-keyword-lists/{listId}/keywords`](/ad-accounts/replace-ad-negative-keyword-list-keywords) replaces the full desired set. Changes apply atomically and affect every attached campaign. Unchanged criteria retain their IDs.
4. [`GET /v1/ads/campaigns/{campaignId}/negative-keyword-lists`](/ad-campaigns/list-campaign-negative-keyword-lists) reads attachments. [`PUT` on that path](/ad-campaigns/replace-campaign-negative-keyword-lists) replaces the full `listIds` set, up to 20 lists from the same Google customer. An empty array detaches all lists without deleting their keywords.
5. Detach a list from every campaign before [`DELETE /v1/ads/accounts/negative-keyword-lists/{listId}`](/ad-accounts/delete-ad-negative-keyword-list).

Shared-list reads are cached for 10 minutes. When Google throttles the request, they can fall back to the last successful copy for up to seven days.

Check `cachedAt` and `stale` before treating the result as current.

## Keyword Planner: ideas

Call `POST /v1/ads/keywords/ideas` with seed keywords, a seed URL, or both. It runs Keyword Planner's idea generation.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: ideas } = await zernio.adinsights.generateKeywordIdeas({
  body: {
    accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d',
    seedKeywords: ['platform engineering tools'],
    seedUrl: 'https://example.com/platform',
    countries: ['US', 'GB'],
    pageSize: 50
  }
});

console.log(ideas.data);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
ideas = client.ad_insights.generate_keyword_ideas(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    seed_keywords=["platform engineering tools"],
    seed_url="https://example.com/platform",
    countries=["US", "GB"],
    page_size=50,
)

print(ideas["data"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/ads/keywords/ideas" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    "seedKeywords": ["platform engineering tools"],
    "seedUrl": "https://example.com/platform",
    "countries": ["US", "GB"],
    "pageSize": 50
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`), rows in Google's raw shape:

```json
{
  "customerId": "1234567890",
  "data": [
    {
      "text": "internal developer platform",
      "keywordIdeaMetrics": {
        "avgMonthlySearches": "2400",
        "competition": "MEDIUM",
        "competitionIndex": "48",
        "lowTopOfPageBidMicros": "1250000",
        "highTopOfPageBidMicros": "6800000",
        "monthlySearchVolumes": [ { "year": "2026", "month": "DECEMBER", "monthlySearches": "2900" } ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "paging": { "nextPageToken": "CAoQ..." }
}
```

## Keyword Planner: historical metrics

Call `POST /v1/ads/keywords/historical-metrics` with exact keywords you already have (up to 1,000 per call).

It returns historical search volume, competition and top-of-page bid ranges, plus `averageCpcMicros` when `includeAverageCpc` is set.

```json
{
  "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
  "keywords": ["internal developer platform", "platform engineering tools"],
  "countries": ["US"],
  "includeAverageCpc": true
}
```

The response has the same `customerId` and `data` shape as ideas, with no `paging`. Historical metrics is a single batch.

## Keyword Planner rules

Both Planner calls above share these.

They do not apply to `GET /v1/ads/keywords`, which returns Zernio's synced rows with numeric counters.

- Rows come back verbatim from Google.
- Counters are int64s encoded as strings. Parse them before doing math.
- Every bid or CPC value is in micros of the account currency. Divide by 1,000,000.
- `countries` omitted means worldwide. `languageConstantId` picks the language (`1000` is English).
- `customerId` is only needed when the connection has several Google Ads accounts.
- Paging: `pageSize` plus `pageToken` from `paging.nextPageToken` (ideas only).

## If it fails

The Keyword Planner calls and the keyword writes on this page run live against Google. They pass the per-user burst limit of 15 requests a minute ([quotas](/platforms/google-ads/reference#quotas-and-the-ops-budget)).

- A `429` with `details.budgetScope: "account"` or `"user"` clears within the minute.
- A `429` with `details.quotaExhausted: true` is Google's quota. Wait until `details.resetsAt`.

Back off before retrying. See [rate limits](/guides/rate-limits) for the general rule.
